label: VERIFIED
extraction: Loop Design Check red-line premise: two levels of feedback. Execution level (low): machine/agent measures 'how far from literal goal' and grinds it to zero - machine is strong here. Judgment level (high): human decides 'is this goal itself right, should it change, should it stop' - machine can't step outside its own loop to question the goal. Thermostat analogy: can feed back 'how far from 26°C', but when you have fever and want 28°C it can't judge whether 26 is right target - just grinds toward 26. 'What to set today' is always human's call. Handing judgment/sign-off/last switch to machine = removing high-level feedback = sprints fast and hard toward goal no one questioned -> wrong output. Three red lines: 1) Keep judgment with human (acceptance/done cell flipped by human, loop not acceptance officer), 2) Responsibility doesn't transfer (can't afford failure -> don't hand over authority automatically), 3) Counter-intuitive warning (more self-improving/rewrites-own-rules -> stricter human review needed, not looser; machine too fast to intercept after the fact, human judgment must sit BEFORE action as hard gate, not post-hoc patch).
